- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 10d avg), model often overshoots — reduce forecast 1–2 days post-spike to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underperforms — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast to counteract mean reversion bias.
- For 30d horizon, model often lags 1–2 days behind true trend — adjust forecast to align with 10d moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model tends to overestimate — cap forecast at 1.5x prior 10d high to avoid overbought bias.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often underestimates — add 0.3–0.7 to forecast to capture hidden momentum.
